details.canonical_statement: No finite simple undirected graph on 62 vertices with maximum degree at most 8 and diameter at most 2 has actual positive-repeat-support components C,K,L of sizes 8,24,30 whose original adjacency quotient in that order is [[2,6,0],[2,1,5],[0,4,4]].

proof_obligations.verification: **Actual identities** (26–37). The degree bound proves regularity; the actual definition of B gives its diagonal, nonnegative off-diagonal entries, symmetry, row sum 3, and commutation. No independent matrix realizability is assumed.

**Closed triangle component** (44–46). The dependency's S_TOUCH contradiction uses only forced saturated unit rows, not global simplicity. Triangle mates avoid the original triangle neighborhood, are distinct by commutation, and themselves form a triangle by nonnegativity. Both triangles' six rows are exhausted, and the prism is connected.

**Triangle-free G** (53–55). A triangle would force an actual support component of size 6. The three actual components have sizes 8,24,30 and cover all 62 vertices, excluding that possibility. Thus Buv=0 on every original edge.

**Actual equitable quotient** (10–11,39–41). Symmetric row-sum-3 B has eigenvalue-3 vectors exactly constant on support components, by its nonnegative energy identity. AB=BA preserves that space, so A applied to every component indicator is constant on each actual component. The stated R therefore supplies genuine per-vertex neighbor counts.

**No weight-three entry** (47). A weight-three entry exhausts both rows and makes its two endpoints a closed two-vertex support component. None of the stipulated components has size 2. Thus B≤2 follows directly in this quotient case; the global triple-repeat theorem is unnecessary.

**Coverage of a double root** (47–48). At an endpoint 0 of a double repeat, its row is 2e_w+e_a and it is triangle-free. Every outside vertex has at least one parent; the actual row gives exactly the parent triple P(w), parent pair P(a), and otherwise single parents. Their intersection sizes 0,1,2 yield D0,D1,D2. Original adjacency w~a is possible only in the disjoint case; its remaining repeat label is BIN or BOUT. The read saturated-row proofs exclude D2 and BIN. This applies to an arbitrary chosen double edge, not merely an existential root.

**D0 support size 4** (48,56). The read D0 proofs force two further distinct vertices and complete rows forming an alternating 2,1,2,1 cycle. All four rows are saturated; this is exactly a closed component, so a double edge in C cannot be D0.

**D1 quotient orientations** (48–51). In raw D1 notation, B1=e2+e3+e4 places 1,2,3,4 in the generated-triangle component J. Vertex 0 in the heavy component H has these four original neighbors. Vertex 1 has the distinct neighbors 0,w,a in H. Equitability gives rHJ≥4 and rJH≥3 when H≠J, or rHH≥4 when equal.

**B[C] is simple** (55–59). For a D1 heavy edge in C, J=C contradicts rCC=2<4; J=K contradicts the correctly oriented reverse entry rKC=2<3; J=L contradicts rCL=0<4. D0 and weight 3 have already been excluded. Nonnegative integrality leaves only 0 and 1 in B[C].
**Matching and parents** (63–67). rKK=1 makes the simple induced graph on K a perfect matching; rKC=2 gives two distinct parents in C per vertex. The matching map p is a genuine involution.

**Cross-block equation** (84–87). B[C,K]=0 because C,K are distinct repeat components. A[C,L]=0. Therefore the (C,K) block of A²+A=7I+J+B is exactly DX+XP+X=J; there is no omitted path through L and no identity-matrix term.

**Disjoint closed parent neighborhoods** (89–91). Column v of (D+I)X is the sum of the two closed-neighborhood indicators. Column v of XP is the indicator of F(p(v)), because P is a symmetric matching matrix. The right side is all ones, proving disjointness and the exact complementary pair, without a transpose error.

**Eight-cycle contradiction** (93–103). A simple triangle-free 2-regular graph on 8 vertices is C8 or 2C4. In C8 the two closed neighborhoods are disjoint only at cyclic distance 3 or 4. At distance 3 their complement is an adjacent pair and creates a triangle with p(v). Hence all parents would be antipodal, and the six K-neighbors of each c would also neighbor its antipode. The bound c(c,c′)=1+Bcc′≤4 contradicts c(c,c′)≥6.

**Opposite parent rule in 2C4** (105–115). Two three-element closed neighborhoods within one four-cycle cannot be disjoint. Parents therefore lie in different cycles. Each closed neighborhood omits exactly its opposite within its cycle, proving F(p(v))=o(F(v)).

**Within-cycle repeat entries** (117–121). Adjacent cycle vertices have no common neighbor; opposite vertices have exactly their two cycle neighbors. No K vertex can have two parents in one cycle, and C has no original neighbor in L. The actual common-neighbor identity gives repeat weights 0 and 1 respectively.

**Binary cross matrix and multiplicities** (123–132). Each B[C] row has one unit at its opposite and two units across cycles; symmetry gives both row and column sums 2 of binary M. Cross-cycle parent vertices have no common neighbor in C or L, so their common-neighbor count is exactly mij. They are nonadjacent, giving mij=1+Mij.

**Simultaneous opposite symmetry** (134–136). The bijection p takes the full parent-label class (i,j) onto (i+2,j+2), including multiplicities. Thus mij=mi+2,j+2 and Mij=Mi+2,j+2. No uniqueness is presumed at a label of multiplicity 2.

**Connectedness forces complementary entries** (138–150). If both row ones occupy j,j+2, opposite-label symmetry gives the same ones in row i+2. With the two opposite repeat edges these four vertices form a unit K4, exhausting all four rows. This would be a closed proper component of C. Hence every row has one one in each opposite column pair; interchanging the two actual cycles gives the column counterpart, proving both identities (8).

**Unique opposite representative** (154–164). A binary row of sum 2 has a zero. At Mij=0, mij=1. Simultaneous opposite symmetry also gives mi+2,j+2=1. The opposite class's unique representative is p(v) by the matching rule. Triangle-free G then gives B(v,p(v))=0.

**Weighted parent marginals and orientation** (166–193). Block diagonality of B gives B[C]X=XB[K]. Its (o(ai),v) entry is B(o(ai),ai)+B(o(ai),bj)=1+Mi+2,j=2; the right side is sum over w with o(ai)∈F(w) of Bwv, equal to the displayed Bvw by symmetry. At o(bj), the cross term is Mi,j+2, not Mi+2,j. Both equal 1 at a zero Mij, so both marginals are 2.

**Exact intersection and its zero weight** (195–197). Every K vertex has exactly two parents, one from each cycle. Therefore membership in U∩V is equivalent to the exact opposite parent pair, not merely containing it. MC19 makes this intersection precisely {p(v)} and its repeat weight from v is zero.

**Weighted contradiction and scope** (198–207). Finite inclusion-exclusion gives 2+2=B(v,U∪V)+B(v,p(v)). The second term is zero; nonnegativity bounds the first by B(v,K). Because K is the actual support component containing v, this equals the full row sum 3. Thus 4≤3. The argument allows weight-two entries anywhere in B[K]; no global or K-block simplicity was used.

counterexample_pass.analysis: For heavy component C and generated component K the needed lower bound is rKC≥3, whereas rCK=6 is allowed. The target uses rKC=2, the correct reverse direction. Taking H=J is separately covered by the internal bound, and the remaining L case fails the forward bound rCL≥4.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Collapse a double/triple repeat or its auxiliary points.
counterexample_pass.analysis: A weight-three pair is a closed size-2 component. The D0 proof prevents its auxiliary c-points from coinciding by a row/commutation bound before counting common neighbors, and forces the four heavy/light vertices to be distinct. The resulting size-4 component cannot be embedded as a proper connected subset of the stipulated C with extra positive edges.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Use an alternative original cycle type.
counterexample_pass.analysis: A triangle-free simple 2-regular eight-vertex graph has no component of order below 4; the only cycle decompositions are 8 and 4+4. On C8, parents {0,3} have complementary pair {5,6}, which is adjacent. Parents {0,4} avoid that triangle but force the six-common-neighbor contradiction. Cyclic distances 1 and 2 already violate closed-neighborhood disjointness.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Place both parents in one C4.
counterexample_pass.analysis: Each closed neighborhood has size 3 in a set of size 4, so overlap is unavoidable. Hence no extra K common neighbor can invalidate the claimed within-cycle repeat counts.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Concentrate a row of M on an opposite pair.
counterexample_pass.analysis: For example, ones at (0,0),(0,2) force ones at (2,0),(2,2). Together with a0a2 and b0b2, this creates the closed unit K4. Dropping connectedness would indeed admit this local pattern; connectedness is part of the actual-component hypothesis and is used explicitly.

Such a label has multiplicity 2, so a uniqueness assertion there would be invalid. The proof deliberately chooses a zero label, whose existence and multiplicity 1 were proved. Matching both copies in multiplicity-2 classes does not affect the zero-label argument.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Use a heavy repeat inside K to cover both marginals.
counterexample_pass.analysis: Arbitrary nonnegative integral repeat weights in K are permitted. A common supplier of the two parent marginals must lie in U∩V={p(v)}, whose weight is exactly zero. Heavy weights at different suppliers are still charged to the same total row budget 3, so cannot supply the required total 4.

Since vp(v) is an actual original edge, B(v,p(v)) counts its common neighbors. A positive value would create a forbidden original triangle; the proof has already established triangle-freeness from component sizes.

counterexample_pass.attempt: Interpret C,K,L as arbitrary cells rather than support components.
counterexample_pass.analysis: This would break block diagonality, the connectedness argument, and the final row-budget equality. The theorem explicitly concerns actual support components; these properties were checked wherever used. No matrix relaxation is substituted for a graph.
